name: clickables

operatingThreshold.rule: the lowest threshold whose precision on the out-of-fold predictions is at least 50% (with at least 5 elements flagged); if none reaches 50%, there is no threshold and no suggestions. The test websites are never used to choose it

selection.rule: the candidate with the highest out-of-fold PR-AUC in 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website on the development sites; the test sites are never used to choose
selection.reason: Highest out-of-fold PR-AUC (0.244) of the 5 candidates in 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website.

crossValidation.rule: the candidate with the highest out-of-fold PR-AUC in 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website on the development sites; the test sites are never used to choose

architecture: gradient-boosted trees over 92 features (300 trees, up to 15 leaves each), temperature-calibrated

data.note: Tranco top-1,000 crawl. Every row from pages with document-level (delegated) click listeners was removed, whatever its label, and landmarks and page regions are not candidates.

comparisons.model: Rule: pointer cursor and not native

seeds.rule: the seeds are candidates like the others, compared by out-of-fold PR-AUC; test scores are never used
seeds.note: test PR-AUC of the graph network trained with each seed, in seed order

beats_best_gbt.target: the graph network beats the best gradient-boosting baseline
beats_best_gbt.note: a gradient-boosting model was chosen by out-of-fold PR-AUC, so no graph network ships

latency.target: <= 50 ms for 2,000 elements in the Web Worker
latency.note: 10 runs in the app's Web Worker (median reported); Google Chrome 151.0.7922.137 (/usr/bin/google-chrome), headless; CPU: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1255U, 12 logical cores; no CPU throttling

summary: The model is experimental and switched off by default. Its suggestions are advisory and never change the score, the history or the report.

Earlier results were inflated by label leakage. The earlier training filter dropped rows from pages with delegated (document-level) click listeners only when their label was 0, and kept every positive. Counting the raw crawl by page type and label showed that it kept 8,691 positives from delegated pages and only 60 from other pages, while every negative it kept came from a non-delegated page, so the page type gave the label away. The filter now drops whole delegated pages, whatever their labels, and every number on this card comes from that corrected run.

There are only 55 trustworthy positives, from 13 websites; one website (capcut.com) has 32 of them. The test websites hold 6, from 2 websites, so the 95% intervals below cover nearly the whole range from 0 to 1. This run cannot measure how good the model is.

The model and its threshold were chosen by 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website on the 115 development websites (49 positives), never on the test websites. The chosen model is element-only gradient boosting (out-of-fold PR-AUC 0.244). Its threshold, 0.111, is the lowest with at least 50% precision on the out-of-fold predictions.

On the 2,559 test elements the model makes 10 suggestions, 3 of them correct: precision 30% and recall 50% (3 of 6), each with a 95% interval from 0% to 100%. Precision is below the 90% the ship gate asks for, so that gate is not met, and the model stays off by default.
failurePatterns: The errors have not been reviewed by hand. errors.json holds all 7 false positives and all 3 false negatives on the test websites at the shipped threshold. Six of the false positives are layout wrappers on one website (booking.com), and one is a page's root <div id="root"> scored 0.91; the 3 misses are accordion toggles on one website (mega.co.nz), scored 0.014. With only 2 test websites holding click-only controls, these are observations, not established patterns.
limitations: The Tranco top-1,000 crawl produced 1,407 page records; 879 pages were used. After every row from delegated pages and every landmark or page region (<main>, <nav>, <header>…) was removed, 9,367 candidate rows from 136 websites remain, and only 13 of those websites have any click-only control. Removing landmarks also removed 5 positives on <nav> and <header> elements.

The candidates scored close together out of fold (0.244, 0.240, 0.207, 0.207 and 0.156), and one website holds 32 of the 49 development positives, all in one fold, so the choice of model is not clear-cut.
All examples come from the Tranco crawl. The corpus has no Vue or Angular pages, and the results are not representative of other kinds of websites.

labelProbe.method: Random sample of labelled candidates; each clicked once at its centre in the live page. "responds": the DOM, address or a dialog changed within 400 ms. Skipped as untestable: pages that change by themselves, and elements whose centre is a link or button. A response can still come from a handler on an ancestor, so disagreement is an upper bound on label noise.

labelHandCheck.method: Method (ml/README.md, step 2): labels/sheet.mjs drew 300 random labelled elements; labels/audit.mjs re-checked each one in the live page with Chrome's DevTools Protocol, reading the element's own listeners and React handlers, its ancestors' and any document-level (delegated) listeners, and marked it correct, wrong or unsure; labels/score.mjs counted the verdicts. The check is automated: an independent manual review by the owner has not been done.
labelHandCheck.reading: This measures whether the labels are accurate, and that still holds after the filter change, because filtering removes rows but does not change any label. It does not fix the small number of positives: only 4 of the judged labels were positive, and the corrected corpus has only 60.
